Episode evidence: T32-E1; T32-E3; T55-E2; recovery and abort discussions
Proposed mechanism: Once an irreversible physical prefix executes, diagnosis and safe reconciliation require command–state–material evidence.
Alternative explanation: Threads about severe execution failures naturally mention both logging and recovery.
Counterexample / limit: Bounded custom abort handling can recover material without complete general observability.
Construct independence: High — observability and recovery are distinct constructs.
Current status: Strong descriptive association and strong mechanism evidence.
Prospective falsifier: In a prospective incident set, recovery time and salvage should not improve with higher event-linkage completeness.
Prospective metric: Observability Coverage versus verified-safe-state time, salvage rate, and disposition completeness.
Forum references: Error catching for composite functions; VENUS feature requests; Return volume after method abort
Publication-safe conclusion: In the pilot, observability and recovery co-occur strongly; the incidents support a mechanism in which incomplete execution evidence constrains safe recovery.

Episode evidence: T04-E2; T37-E3; T38-E1; contamination and TADM cases
Proposed mechanism: Telemetry, state histories, and traces become scientifically useful only after acceptance rules and claim boundaries are defined.
Alternative explanation: Validation discussions often request more observations, making directionality bidirectional.
Counterexample / limit: Rich telemetry can remain weak evidence when starting conditions or ground truth are missing.
Construct independence: High — evidence availability and claim alignment are separable.
Current status: Strong descriptive association; direction remains bidirectional.
Prospective falsifier: Additional observability fields fail to improve agreement on whether a claim is supported.
Prospective metric: OC versus Test–Claim Alignment, adjudicator agreement, and diagnosis latency.
Forum references: Automation Report Data; TADM curves; contamination tracking; VerisFlow
Publication-safe conclusion: Observability is frequently coupled to validation, but telemetry volume alone does not determine claim validity.

Episode evidence: T05-E1–E3; scheduler comparison and open-scheduler discussions
Proposed mechanism: A scheduler's usable action space is constrained by the devices it can invoke, observe, reserve, and maintain.
Alternative explanation: Scheduler threads are purposively selected for device breadth and deployment questions.
Counterexample / limit: A fully accessible device interface does not establish scheduling quality or optimization capability.
Construct independence: High — interface accessibility and scheduling capability are distinct.
Current status: Strong descriptive association and plausible enabling condition.
Prospective falsifier: Scheduler performance remains unchanged when driver reachability, state observability, and simulator availability are degraded.
Prospective metric: IAS versus executable-device coverage, failed dispatches, integration time, and benchmark completion.
Forum references: User feedback on Schedulers; Open source scheduler; Galago
Publication-safe conclusion: The forum evidence supports interface accessibility as an enabling condition for orchestration, not as a measure of scheduler quality.

Episode evidence: T04-E1–E3; T21-E1–E3; lid and imported-resource discussions
Proposed mechanism: Physical definitions acquire credibility through measurement, simulation, hardware testing, and independent reproduction.
Alternative explanation: Troubleshooting a bad definition necessarily generates validation discussion.
Counterexample / limit: A resource may be well specified but used outside its validated device/configuration envelope.
Construct independence: High — representation completeness and evidence grade are related but non-identical.
Current status: Moderate-to-strong descriptive association with direct incident support.
Prospective falsifier: Higher evidence grades do not reduce cross-machine definition failures or improve test–claim alignment.
Prospective metric: PDC/evidence grade versus cross-machine success, correction rate, and TCA.
Forum references: 50 µL tip post-mortem; PLR z-height; lid definitions; Opentrons imports
Publication-safe conclusion: Physical-resource discussions consistently show that geometry values require provenance and bounded validation before portability claims are justified.

Episode evidence: T37-E1–E4; T38-E1–E3; AI-method and AI-validation discussions
Proposed mechanism: AI-generated methods create an evaluation funnel in which syntactic, simulated, dry, wet, and assay performance must be reported separately.
Alternative explanation: B9 has only five coded threads and was deliberately sampled around AI evaluation.
Counterexample / limit: AI can be valuable for prototyping even when downstream validation remains human-led.
Construct independence: High — AI involvement and evaluation-stage specification are distinct.
Current status: Strong within the small B9 stratum; highly sample-sensitive.
Prospective falsifier: AI-generated methods reach wet and assay validation without increased acceptance-rule or evidence requirements.
Prospective metric: Validation-stage depth, human correction burden, wet-pass rate, and claim calibration.
Forum references: AI Assisted Method Writing; VerisFlow v0.4; AI in Lab Automation
Publication-safe conclusion: Within the selected AI discussions, evaluation semantics are central; the association should be treated as a focused stratum finding, not a forum-wide rate.
